- **self**: solana-py solders and @solana/web3.js and @solana/kit (7/4)

## Definitions

- [statement] @solana/kit is the renamed 2.x line of @solana/web3.js. It is functional (no classes except SolanaError), fully tree-shakable, uses Web Crypto Ed25519 so key and signing operations are async, supports native bigint, and has zero third-party dependencies. It is not backward-compatible with web3.js 1.x. (high confidence) — https://github.com/anza-xyz/kit · keywords: solana-py solders and @solana/web3.js and @solana/kit · also: https://blog.triton.one/intro-to-the-new-solana-kit-formerly-web3-js-2/, https://www.quicknode.com/guides/solana-development/tooling/web3js/migrate-to-v3
- [statement] Kit has no Connection or Transaction classes. Moving a web3.js v1 codebase to Kit means rewriting every call site, and libraries such as Anchor's TypeScript client did not plug into Kit. The @solana/compat package offers conversion helpers between legacy and Kit types. (high confidence) — https://www.quicknode.com/guides/solana-development/tooling/web3js/migrate-to-v3 · keywords: solana-py solders and @solana/web3.js and @solana/kit · also: https://github.com/anza-xyz/kit

## How it works

- [statement] Guidance after the compromise: upgrade to 1.95.8 (even when pinned to latest) or downgrade to a version before 1.95.6, and rotate any suspect authority keys, including multisigs, program authorities and server keypairs. Cyfrin added: check yarn.lock or package-lock.json for the bad versions, and keep strict version control and lockfiles. (high confidence) — https://anza.xyz/blog/web3-js-exploit-root-cause-analysis · keywords: solana-py solders and @solana/web3.js and @solana/kit · also: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jcxm-7wvp-g6p5, https://www.csoonline.com/article/3617893/solana-sdk-backdoored-for-stealing-secrets-private-keys.html, https://www.cyfrin.io/blog/critical-security-alert-solana-web3-js-library-compromise
- [statement] Anza's root-cause analysis says the phished publisher entered a username and password and completed two-factor authentication on an attacker-run clone of the npm site, so two-factor authentication did not stop the attack. (medium confidence) — https://anza.xyz/blog/web3-js-exploit-root-cause-analysis · keywords: solana-py solders and @solana/web3.js and @solana/kit · also: https://helpnetsecurity.com/2024/12/04/solana-web3-js-supply-chain-compromise
- [statement] In Python, solders (Rust-backed bindings by Kevin Heavey) supplies the core types: Keypair, Pubkey, Instruction, MessageV0, VersionedTransaction, signing and serialization, RPC request and response types, and an in-process LiteSVM. solders does not fetch blockhashes or send transactions; solana-py's AsyncClient does (get_latest_blockhash, send_transaction). solana-py builds on solders types, and its README says anything missing from it 'is probably in solders now'. Solana's docs name both packages and recommend solana-py for networking and async APIs. The solders tutorial recommends versioned transactions 'if you have a choice'. The two install separately (pip install solders; pip install solana). (high confidence) — https://kevinheavey.github.io/solders/tutorials/transactions.html · keywords: solana-py solders and @solana/web3.js and @solana/kit · also: https://github.com/michaelhly/solana-py, https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/clients/community/python.mdx

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Upgrading to web3.js v3 silently changes Connection's default commitment from finalized to confirmed. The code compiles unchanged, so the compiler cannot flag it; the official migration guide says 'omitted commitment now defaults to confirmed rather than finalized'. A bot that relied on finalized reads must pass the commitment explicitly on the Connection or per call, and should test against a real node because mocked tests keep passing with the old default. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-web3.js/blob/main/packages/web3.js/RELEASE_NOTES.md · keywords: solana-py solders and @solana/web3.js and @solana/kit · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-web3.js/blob/main/docs/web3js-v1-to-v3-migration.md, https://www.quicknode.com/guides/solana-development/tooling/web3js/migrate-to-v3

## Facts and statements

- [statement] In Python, solders (Rust bindings) supplies the core types (Keypair, Pubkey, Instruction, MessageV0, VersionedTransaction), RPC request and response types, and a LiteSVM test VM (solders.litesvm) that Solana's docs call a much faster alternative to solana-test-validator. solders does no networking. solana-py is built on solders and supplies AsyncClient, SolanaWsClient and SPL Token helpers. Solana's docs list both under community clients and recommend solana-py for networking and async RPC. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/clients/community/python.mdx · keywords: solana-py solders and @solana/web3.js and @solana/kit · also: https://github.com/michaelhly/solana-py, https://kevinheavey.github.io/solders/tutorials/transactions.html, https://github.com/kevinheavey/solders/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
